successors.note: The Ming split the Mong Mao territory into smaller states; the remnant under Si Jifa at Möng Yang was attacked in 1449.

capitals.name: Selan (Nam Mao valley, near Ruili)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Selan', 'most often adopted', built by Hsö Hkan Hpa c. 1335; 'various capitals located around the Nam Mao valley'; the capital fell in 1442 and 1444; Möng Yang from 1442 for Si Renfa.

rulers.name: Si Kefa
rulers.note: Hsö Hkan Hpa; infobox 'becomes ruler of Möng Mao: c. 1335'.

rulers.name: Si Lunfa
rulers.note: Surrendered in 1388; deposed in 1397 and restored in 1398 (the table gives his reign 1382-1399).

rulers.name: Si Renfa
rulers.note: Table 1413-1445/6, executed (clipped to 1444, the end of the state); the infobox 1413-1442. His son Si Jifa (1445/6) held Möng Yang until the fourth Ming campaign of 1449.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Möng Mao row; its Shan States row holds the Yunnan part, 106 cells of the 1294 shape, 93 of them dropped in 1385). The page names the Nam Mao valley (Ruili), Selan, Hsenwi and Kale and says the territory 'extends for 10,000 li' (Baiyi Zhuan, 1396), so the Yunnan core is the minimum; the extent west of the Salween (Mogaung, Mohnyin, Bhamo) is not on the page. Infobox/page area: none.

ledger.note: 1256: the Möng Mao ruling line begins. 'Per Jiang Yingliang, the ruler lineage commenced in 1256'; the Luchuan Route of the Yuan was set up here in 1276 ('Möng Mao was designated as Luchuan Route') and the Tai 'pledged allegiance to the Yuan dynasty as early as 1260'. Hsö Hkan Hpa 'becomes ruler of Möng Mao: c. 1335' and builds Selan.

ledger.note: 1442: the Ming take the capital. After campaigns in 1438 and 1441, 'Möng Mao's capital fell in 1442, and Si Renfa fled to Möng Yang with his family'. A third campaign in 1443.

ledger.note: 1444: Möng Mao is defeated. 'Möng Mao's capital was captured again in 1444'; a fourth campaign against Si Jifa at Möng Yang follows in 1449.

ledger.note: 1444: Möng Mao ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1444'; its Yunnan lands pass to the Ming, its remnant to Möng Yang. The shan-states dossier has the Ming take the Yunnan lands in 1444 and a boundary stone set on the Irrawaddy after the 1449 peace.

sources.title: Möng Mao

notes: State Cliopatria lacks as such: its Shan States row (1294-1563) holds the Yunnan part. The shan-states dossier (se-01-e) keeps Möng Mao inside the Shan States outline and its Yunnan lands to 1444 (a 1385 correction), and named Möng Mao as a counterpart needing a dossier; this dossier uses the same region, so the renderer sees two claims on the Yunnan cells 1385-1444 and a gap-filler should drop them from one. One page opened (budget 2-5). Not settled: (1) three dates for the start: 1256 (Jiang Yingliang's line), 1276 (Luchuan Route under the Yuan), c. 1335 (Hsö Hkan Hpa); the Möng Mao page has no 1253 founding; (2) the page says Hsenwi and Kale were within reach and the Baiyi Zhuan gives 10,000 li, but names no frontier, so the Burmese-side extent is not drawn; (3) the status years under the Yuan (Pingmian commissioner, infobox 1355-1384) and the Ming (Luchuan-Pingmian commission 1384-1441) are vassalages whose pairs belong to yuan-dynasty and ming-dynasty; (4) the 1356 Sagaing expedition and the 1364 fall of 'the two kingdoms' (Sagaing and Pinya) are on the page without a territorial result for Möng Mao and are not in the ledger; (5) Möng Yang (Si Jifa's remnant, to 1449) is not a dossier.
